definition: A picture of a sample space as a rectangle, with each event drawn as a circle inside it; where circles overlap, the outcomes belong to both events.

A diagram with one set of branches for each stage of an experiment, where the branches from each point add up to $1$; you multiply along a path and add across paths, and a later branch can carry a probability that depends on the earlier one.
The event $A \cup B$, read "$A$ or $B$": at least one of $A$ and $B$ happens, including when both happen.
Events that cannot both happen, so $\mathrm{P}(A \cap B) = 0$; this is not the same as being independent.
The probability of $A$ given that $B$ has happened, written $\mathrm{P}(A \mid B)$ and equal to $\frac{\mathrm{P}(A \cap B)}{\mathrm{P}(B)}$, where $\mathrm{P}(B) > 0$.

Events where one happening does not change the probability of the other, so $\mathrm{P}(A \cap B) = \mathrm{P}(A)\,\mathrm{P}(B)$; two mutually exclusive events that each have a non-zero probability are never independent.
Choosing items one after another without putting each one back, so the total, and the probabilities for the next pick, change after every pick.
